Moreover, we are also of the conviction that this uniformity has certain functional benefits. Freight forwarders often utilize local cartage firms operating pursuant to the section 203(b)(8) exemption to effectuate collection and delivery services. Disparate areas of operation would force these carriers to separate shipments according to distance and would generally interfere with the flexibility of these carriers' operations. There would also be considerable difficulty in monitoring the operations of these exempt motor carriers if they could serve non-identical geographic areas under sections 202(c) and 203(b)(8).
The freight forwarder comments on the Interim Report evidence a great concern with the treatment to be accorded their terminals and TOFC ramps at suburban locations in the New York City-New Jersey area. This issue is better addressed in a specific discussion of the New York, N.Y., commercial zone and is reserved for a subsequent section of this report.
